sentences.text:
Hon'ble Mr. Justice Deepak Kumar Tiwari Order On Board 20/2/2023 1. Heard.
2.

This petition has been filed by the petitioner for quashing of FIR No.462/2018 registered at Police Station Durg, District Durg (CG) for the offence under Sections 294, 506 of IPC and Sections 66(e),
67 of the Information and Technology Act and further, the consequential criminal proceedings pursuant to the impugned FIR in Criminal Case No.33345/2018 pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Durg.
3.

Brief facts of the case are that complainant Yogeshwar Meshram has lodged an FIR alleging that the petitioner had attached an obscene photograph, depicting the complainant in a comprising position with a lady, to the e-mail of the complainant as also of his friend.
Based on such e-mail, the petitioner threatened the complainant and asked him to meet her.

Thereafter, the petitioner lodged an FIR against the complainant at Police Station Santacruz, Mumbai under Sections 376, 354,
506(2), 417 of IPC, in which, the complainant was enlarged on anticipatory bail.

On the basis of such information, the Police registered an offence against the petitioner under the aforementioned Sections and after completion of the investigation, charge sheet has been filed before the CJM, Durg.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the continuation of the criminal proceedings would amount to abuse of the process of law.
There is no material on record which prima facie shows that the petitioner has sent any obscene photograph from her e-mail ID.
Since the complaint has been lodged as a counter blast, therefore, learned counsel prays to quash the impugned FIR and the consequential criminal proceedings.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the State submits that there is sufficient material available on record to constitute the aforementioned offence, for which, the charge sheet has already been filed.
He submits that the submission put-forth by learned counsel for the petitioner is required to be seen during trial.

sentences.text: 6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents annexed along with the petition with utmost circumspection.

7. In Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and others, 2021 SCC OnLine SC 315, it has been categorically held by Hon'ble the Supreme Court that while examining an FIR/complaint, quashing of which is sought, the court cannot embark upon an enquiry as to the reliability or genuineness or otherwise of the allegations made in the FIR/complaint; criminal proceedings ought not to be scuttled at the initial stage; and quashing of a complaint/FIR should be an exception and a rarity than an ordinary rule.
8.

entities.text: Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and others, 2021 SCC OnLine SC 315
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having considered the aforesaid principle laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court and also considering the material available on record, this Court is of the view that the present is not a fit case for quashment of the FIR and the subsequent criminal proceedings.
9. The petition being bereft of any merit, is liable to be and is hereby dismissed.
